## SECTION 1 — BUSINESS & COMPETITIVE POSITION

**Business.** Dynatrace is an AI-powered observability platform: application/cloud monitoring, log management, digital experience, security, and AI-driven automation (Grail data lakehouse, Davis AI, agentic automation). ~$2.14B ARR (Q1 FY2027, +17%), high recurring subscription mix ($530M of $555M quarterly revenue). **Moat:** sticky, mission-critical enterprise platform with high switching costs; 16 consecutive years as a Gartner MQ Leader; AI-workload customers consume ~1.5× non-AI customers; log consumption ~$200M annualized, doubling in two quarters (Q1 FY2027 release). **Moat is "real but limited"** [web research brief]: Datadog grows faster (~32%) and is far larger; New Relic and AppDynamics compete on price; open-source (Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry) pressures standardization; DPS consumption-based pricing is a deliberate shift to a more flexible model that could aid adoption but adds revenue-timing variability.

**Assessment:** A high-quality compounder with a defensible but contested position. This is not a "wide moat at any price" name — the moat is real, but the pricing/competitive pressure and the need to continuously out-innovate on AI are material. Net-net: quality of the business is above average; certainty of the *magnitude and duration* of growth is below the multiple the market pays.

---

## SECTION 2 — FINANCIAL HISTORY & QUALITY

**Growth (filed):** Revenue $0.398B (FY2018) → $2.018B (FY2026); 5-yr revenue CAGR **+23.5%** [pack, arithmetic]. Recent YoY deceleration: FY2024 +23.3%, FY2025 +18.7%, FY2026 +18.8%, Q1 FY2027 +16%, FY2027 guided +14.6% (cc +14.5–15%). Trend is a disciplined, visible deceleration from mid-20s toward mid-teens — classic SaaS maturity curve. Note the Q1 FY2027 call's claim of "four consecutive quarters of acceleration in TTM organic net new ARR" (+66% net new ARR, +41% organic) — the company's *leading indicator* is improving even as reported revenue growth rounds down. This is the single most important bull counterweight.

**Profitability (filed):**
- GAAP operating margin: 12.2% (latest) vs 8.8% median over 9 years — improving.
- Non-GAAP operating margin: ~30% (FY2026), 29% Q1 FY2027, guided 29.5–29.75% FY2027.
- **SBC is the whole story between GAAP and non-GAAP:** FY2026 SBC $300M = 14.9% of revenue, vs GAAP net income $163M (8.1% margin). Owner earnings (OCF − SBC − capex) = $230M = 11.4% of revenue.
- FY2025 net income of $484M is a **one-time tax-benefit artifact** (the Dec-2024 quarter printed $362M net income on $436M revenue — an ~83% net margin that is not operational). FY2026's $163M is the normal run-rate. Trailing P/E of 99 is therefore both "correct on GAAP" and "a distorted multiple to anchor on."
- Cash conversion is strong *before* SBC: OCF margin 27.8% (FY2026), 55% of revenue in Q1 FY2027 (seasonal). After SBC, still healthy.

**Quality metrics [pack, §7]:** Piotroski 6/8, accruals ratio −0.093 (favorable — earnings backed by cash), no split suspected, net issuance +0.0% (1-yr), capex-light (~1.6% of revenue). D&A jumped from $13M (FY2023) to $55M (FY2024) then $24M (FY2026) — an unresolved tag/definition wobble in the extract, but immaterial to a cash-flow valuation (OCF already nets it).

**Summary:** Financially clean, cash-generative, capex-light, improving GAAP margins, with one disclosed quality issue that dominates the gap between headline and true economics: **$300M+/yr of SBC.**

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION ENGINE SELECTION & METHODOLOGY

**Primary engine: 10-year explicit DCF on Owner Earnings (FCFE-equivalent), + Gordon terminal value.**

Cash-flow definition (the decision that matters most):
- **Owner earnings = OCF − SBC − capex.** Rationale, per the pack's own instruction (§5 note): OCF adds back SBC, so not subtracting it overstates distributable cash flow to existing shareholders. With ~$300M/yr SBC vs $163M GAAP net income, this is a *first-order* adjustment, not a refinement.
- **Cross-check (upper bound): as-reported adjusted FCF = OCF − capex** (the company's own guided metric: $610–615M FY2027, 26.5% margin), without subtracting SBC. This is the sell-side convention. It is defensible *only to the extent* the $1B buyback program offsets dilution — which it currently does (see §9). The truth for a per-share owner sits between the two; I present both and weight toward the SBC-adjusted view per the framework's data-discipline rule.

**Why DCF and not a multiple:** A 15%-grower with a 99x GAAP P/E is only comprehensible through cash flows; the non-GAAP P/E (24x) and EV/S (5.7x) cross-checks hide the SBC issue. The DCF makes the assumptions explicit. **Cross-checks:** forward non-GAAP P/E, EV/S vs peers, and reverse-DCF (implied discount rate).

**Why 10 years:** The company guides only through FY2027. Beyond that I build a transparent glide and stress it (§8) rather than pretending a multi-year path is knowable. Terminal growth 3.0% ≈ long-run nominal GDP [Assumption]; terminal OE margin 18.5% (see §4).

## SECTION 7 — EXPECTATIONS GAP (WHAT IS PRICED IN)

That is *below* the vendor's own 0.711 beta and far below what a 15%-grower with 99x trailing GAAP P/E and 49x owner earnings deserves.

Equivalently, on my 9.0% base CoE, the market is paying for **roughly the Rule-of-50 bull path at an ~8.5% discount rate** (bull-case EV ≈ $13.6B at 8.5% vs. market EV $13.2B). Put plainly:

> **The current price embeds (a) successful execution of the activist's aggressive FY2029 "Rule of 50" margin program, (b) sustained ~14–15% growth for several years, AND (c) a sub-8.5% discount rate. Miss on any one of the three and the stock reverts toward $32–42.**

The expectations gap on quality-adjusted earnings is **negative**: price exceeds my fair value by ~25% (base) to ~5% (bull). The market is effectively ignoring the SBC reality and discounting DT as a ~0.7-beta compounder. There is no margin of safety at $49.12 on my primary basis.

## SECTION 9 — BALANCE SHEET, NET DEBT & CAPITAL ALLOCATION

- **Net cash ≈ $1,060M.** I deliberately include the investments columns (excluding them would flip the sign of my judgment on leverage, per pack §12) and I do *not* double-count the lease line.

**Capital allocation — the SBC/buyback tension (central to this name):**
- SBC is a genuine $300M+/yr cost. But in FY2027 the company is buying back **$275M in Q1 alone** (7.1M shares at $38.88) under a **$1B authorization** [Actual, IR 2026-08-05], with Starboard pressing for **$2.5B of returns over ~3 years** [web, WSJ/Reuters via US News, April 2026] and guided diluted shares falling from 303.7M (FY2026) to 295–297M (FY2027).

On a per-share basis this partially rehabilitates the as-reported-FCF view (upper bound ~$61 at 9%). **However**, buying back at $49+ (near or above my intrinsic) transfers value *from* remaining shareholders; only the $38.88 Q1 repurchases were accretive to my model. Continued buybacks above ~$40 would be value-dilutive per my base case.
- Net cash will be drawn down to fund the buyback program ($1B authorization vs ~$612M FY2027 adj-FCF), which my equity bridge handles by using current net cash + current shares (a conservative steady-state approximation).

## SECTION 11 — DATA QUALITY & LIMITATIONS

1. **SBC treatment is the valuation's fulcrum, and the pack's own instruction (§5) supports my primary (subtract SBC) choice.** The full honest range: **$37** (owner earnings, 9% CoE) to **$61** (as-reported FCF, 9% CoE, buybacks offsetting dilution). Anyone using the upper end must simultaneously believe the $1B+ buyback program persists indefinitely *and* is executed below intrinsic value.
2. **Post-FY2027 forecast is entirely [Assumption].** FY2027 is company-grounded; FY2028+ revenue growth, margin path, terminal margin, and terminal growth are my construction. The §8 sensitivity table is the honest answer to "what if I'm wrong" — the conclusion (no margin of safety at $49.12 at CoE ≥ 8.5%) is stable across scenarios.
3. **FY2025 GAAP net income ($484M) is distorted by a one-time tax benefit** — do not use it as a base; FY2026's $163M is the run-rate.
4. **Beta is unverified** (vendor, unstated window, 0.711). My base uses 1.0; the report shows the full 0.75–1.15 / 7.5–10.5% range so the reader can apply their own view. At beta 0.75 the stock is roughly fairly valued; at beta 1.0 it is ~25% overvalued.
5. Segment revenue/margins are absent from the pack (zero dimensional rows) — no SOTP possible; valuation rests on consolidated DCF.
6. Effective tax rate withheld; I embedded ~15% cash tax on incremental margin as an [Assumption] inside the OE-margin path (not a separate line), so it is not over-fit.
7. Analyst Q&A (where guidance gets pinned down) is not held; the Investor Day (Nov 2026) is the next real data point on the Rule-of-50 path.

**The reasoning in one page:**
1. **The earnings that matter are ~$230–290M/yr, not $530–612M.** The pack is explicit that OCF must be reduced by SBC ($300M/yr, 15% of revenue) for owner earnings. On that basis, DT trades at **~49x FY2027 owner earnings** — a price that only makes sense at a ~7.5% discount rate, which implies a sub-0.7 beta that contradicts both the business risk and the stock's own realized volatility.
2. **The market is betting on the activist script** — Rule of 50 by FY2029 (≈35% non-GAAP margin), sustained 14–15% growth, sub-8.5% CoE, and a $1B+ buyback executed below intrinsic value. Every element is *plausible*; the combination, fully priced in, is not a margin of safety — it is the bull case selling at the bull-case price.
3. **What would change my mind:** (a) the Investor Day (post-Q2 FY2027, ~Nov 2026) *committing* to a Rule-of-50 margin path and then delivering 2–3 quarters of it; (b) evidence that SBC % of revenue is durably declining below ~10%; (c) a pullback to **$37–42** (where base-case value provides an actual buffer and the buyback becomes accretive rather than dilutive); or (d) a durable reduction in the 10Y to <4% (which mechanically lifts fair value toward the low-$40s).

**Execution stance:** **No position / Underweight.** If already long, this is not a moment to add — the risk/reward at $49.12 is asymmetric to the downside on quality-adjusted cash flows. Revisit on the post-Q2 Investor Day and/or at a price in the $38–42 range.

**The decisive driver is described bluntly:** Dynatrace is an excellent business (strong growth, 110% NRR, 82% gross margin, 30% non-GAAP OM, net cash, real AI tailwinds) **but the market is capitalizing the company on the street’s "adjusted free cash flow," which ignores ~15% of revenue in stock-based compensation.** The pack's own data says that if OCF is the starting point and SBC is not subtracted, owner earnings are overstated. When SBC is subtracted — as it must be for a per-share owner to realize value from the business — the stock is worth roughly $25 at a fair 9.7% discount rate, and even $32 at the vendor's unreasonably-low beta.

**Execution guidance:**
- **Existing holders:** Sell / exit. The only price at which the street's accounting even approaches fair is ~$45.50, and the market is at $49.12; every owner-economics scenario is 20–69% below price.
- **Prospective holders:** Do not initiate. Place a **watch list entry at ≤ $32** (the vendor-beta owner-economics fair value), with a more attractive accumulation zone of **≤ $25** (my base).
- **If forced to hold for tax/benchmark reasons:** At minimum, do not add; set a hard exit if FY28 guidance (due May 2027) shows constant-currency revenue growth below 13% or if Arize integration produces operating-margin dilution beyond the guided 175bps.
- **What would change my mind toward Buy:** (1) SBC as % of revenue sustainably declining toward 10% or below while growth stays ≥15%; (2) management formally guiding FY28 revenue growth ≥15% with non-GAAP OM ≥31%; (3) evidence of durable AI-consumption-driven ARR acceleration (e.g., log management crossing $0.5B ARR with AI cohort growth above 2×); (4) a price at or below $25.

**Final statement:** At $49.12, the market price bakes in a world in which $300M of annual stock-based compensation is free. It is not free. The framework's data-discipline rules — confirmed by the pack's own Section 5 warning — demand that owner earnings start from OCF and subtract SBC. On that basis, Dynatrace is a high-quality name trading at roughly 2× its intrinsic value. **Sell.**

## SECTION 0 - HOW TO READ THIS REPORT

### 12.5 What the market price implies
At $49.12 × 296M shares = $14.54B equity; EV = $14.21B (base net cash).
- **At 8% WACC:** required terminal OE margin = **23.2%** → non-GAAP operating margin ≈ **38%** into perpetuity. Only a handful of software firms in history have sustained that; Dynatrace's own guide is 29.6% for FY27. The price at 8% is pricing in near-best-in-class profitability that management has not guided to or historically demonstrated.
- **At 7% WACC:** required terminal OE margin = **14.7%** → non-GAAP op margin ≈ **29.8%** — basically no margin expansion beyond FY27 guidance. At 7%, the market is paying a fair price for a no-improvement world.

**The entire valuation pivots on the discount rate, not on growth.** Growth beyond FY30 adds little (the terminal value dominates and margin/SBC absorb extra revenue). The 10-year Treasury has risen ~100bp since April 2026 (from ~3.52% to 4.69%). At 8%, the stock is ~18% above my intrinsic value; at 7%, it is approximately fair.
